note: Comment drafts for the outbound queue, written by Claude after studying each post's cover. RULES FOR SAKSHI: (1) Open the post first — the cover is not the whole post; if the content differs, the draft is wrong, adapt or skip. (2) Change at least a few words so it's yours. (3) Never post two drafts verbatim on the same account. (4) SKIP-tagged rows are deliberate — one comment per series. Priorities: HIGH = recent + small like-count = top visibility; LOW = big accounts, comment sits deep.

drafts.post_gist: '1 DAY — that's how long your health insurance lasts after you quit your job' (carousel)
drafts.suggested: This one deserves more noise. The women it hits hardest are the ones planning a career break — so many mums in our workshops assumed the company cover 'carried over' for a few months, and found out mid-break that it ended the day they resigned. If you're planning a break: personal policy FIRST, resignation second — waiting periods don't care about your timing.
drafts.why: Career-break angle is pure IFM territory; post is 2 likes old so this sits at the top permanently.

drafts.post_gist: 'She needed ₹6 lakh to start her business. So she borrowed from people she trusted.'
drafts.suggested: So familiar. Half the women in our workshops funded their first venture exactly this way — family first, bank never. Not because the numbers didn't work, but because walking into a branch felt like being judged. The confidence gap costs more than the interest rate.
drafts.why: The deck's worked example — empathy before expertise. Zero comments there, so IFM is instantly visible.

drafts.post_gist: 'She Made 1.75L Using This Plan' — a woman's plan-based investing win
drafts.suggested: The 'plan' word is doing the heavy lifting here and most people will miss it. The wins we see in our classes are never from picking something clever — they're from a boring plan that survived birthdays, school fees and one scary market month. The plan is the product.
drafts.why: Extends the post's idea with a small position; 18 likes = top-comment visibility.

drafts.post_gist: 'How Independent is Independent India?' — financial-independence-themed Independence Day reel
drafts.suggested: The stat that stays with us: most married women we meet can list the family's investments but aren't a holder on a single one. Independence isn't only having money — it's your name on the paperwork. That second step is the one nobody talks about.
drafts.why: Adds the 'name on the paperwork' angle — concrete, and squarely IFM's message.

drafts.post_gist: Monika Halan with fresh copies of her new book 'Let's Talk Legacy'
drafts.suggested: Congratulations, Monika! 'Let's Talk Money' is the book we most often see dog-eared in our workshop bags — mums pass it to each other like a family recipe. Legacy is the conversation Indian families avoid the longest, so thank you for going there. Which chapter was hardest to write?
drafts.why: Warm congrats + genuine question to an authority figure — relationship-building, and the dog-eared detail is real social proof only IFM could offer.

drafts.post_gist: 'Should I sell my house to unlock capital for retirement?' — Let's Talk Money Q&A
drafts.suggested: The rental-yield test is such a clean way to frame it. The emotional half is harder: for most women we teach, the house isn't an asset, it's the proof of a life's work — so 'sell it' lands like 'undo it'. The reframe that helps: you're not selling the house, you're promoting it to fund the next 30 years.
drafts.why: Engages the actual argument, adds the emotional layer plus a usable reframe. 10 likes = instant visibility.

drafts.post_gist: Personal photo — Neha in wedding-season finery with (likely) her mother
drafts.suggested: The saree-and-sneakers energy of teaching money by day and pulling this off by evening 🙌 Both of you look wonderful — and honestly, finance content needs more of exactly this: real women, real occasions, zero jargon.
drafts.why: Personal posts reward warmth, not expertise. Relationship play with a mid-size creator whose audience overlaps ours.

drafts.post_gist: 'This hack is the easiest way to increase your credit score' — credit-score content
drafts.suggested: The India version of this that shocks our workshop rooms: most married women have never once checked their own CIBIL score — everything runs on the husband's. First homework we set is 'pull your own score tonight.' The number of women who discover they don't have one is the whole lesson.
drafts.why: Localises a US post with a specific India insight and a real classroom ritual.

drafts.post_gist: Tori on publicly committing to saving $100K at 25 before she knew she could do it
drafts.suggested: The public announcement is the underrated part of this story. We see it weekly: the mums who tell their kids the savings goal hit it far more often than the ones who keep it private. Announcing it turns your family into your accountability system — kids are ruthless auditors.
drafts.why: Picks out one mechanism (public commitment) and adds a genuinely charming, IFM-specific observation.

drafts.post_gist: 'Unemployed at 23, millionaire at 27 — the thing that changed everything was a single system'
drafts.suggested: The 'system beats income' point is the one our beginners resist the most — everyone believes they have an earning problem when most have a leaking problem. The women who track one month of spending honestly never argue about it again. The system doesn't need to be clever, it needs to be visible.
drafts.why: Agrees, then sharpens with the earning-vs-leaking distinction — quotable and ours.

drafts.post_gist: Shiprocket IPO details card — dates Aug 12–14, band ₹92–97, lot 154 shares
drafts.suggested: Useful card! For the first-timers reading: lot size 154 × ₹97 is about ₹15,000 — that's the real ticket to play, not ₹97. The number of new investors who learn about lot sizes only at the payment screen is too high. Always multiply before you fall in love with an IPO.
drafts.why: Adds the one beginner calculation the card leaves implicit. Practical, non-competing.

drafts.post_gist: 'AI is just for tech bros!' — a 45-year-old home baker proved them wrong
drafts.suggested: The 45-year-old home baker is every second woman in our workshops — told for decades that tech and money are someone else's department. The pattern we see: it was never ability, it was permission. Once one aunty in the room gets it working, the whole row follows within minutes.
drafts.why: Story-post empathy + the 'permission not ability' line, which is IFM's core belief.

drafts.post_gist: Azaadi series — 'Freedom to Earn: to build a life on my own terms'
drafts.suggested: Lovely series. The freedom that gets discussed least is the one after this: freedom to *decide* what the earning becomes. So many women earn and then hand over the deciding. Earning is step one; staying in the room when the money is discussed is the real azaadi.
drafts.why: ONE comment on this series only (see note) — extends its own metaphor rather than praising it.

drafts.post_gist: '4 finance documentaries that'll teach you more than any course'
drafts.suggested: Adding one for the mums: anything on household inflation beats another market documentary. Watching prices instead of tickers is how most women already think about money — start where the intuition already lives, then bridge to investing.
drafts.why: 4.4K likes — comment will sit deep. Only worth it because the take is genuinely additive. Skip if time-pressed.

drafts.post_gist: Govt giving ₹15K to freshers (ELI scheme explainer with FM clip)
drafts.suggested: The detail freshers miss: this lands through EPFO — which means the real gift is being forced onto payroll with a PF account at 22. The ₹15K is nice; the habit it starts is worth lakhs by 40. First salary + PF statement = the best money lesson there is.
drafts.why: 4.5K likes — deep comment. Take is good; post only if the day's HIGH/MED list is done.

drafts.post_gist: Roxane Gay quote on Rihanna saving something of herself for herself
drafts.suggested: 'Save something of herself for herself' works word-for-word as money advice too — the first thing we teach mums is that paying yourself first isn't selfish, it's structural. Rihanna as a personal-finance framework: unexpectedly sound.
drafts.why: US audience, big account — low priority. Charming if there's time.

drafts.post_gist: Hindi shayari — the world seeks greatness in women, not equality, because equality would mean sharing love, respect and housework equally
drafts.suggested: वाह — आख़िरी line सबसे भारी है 💛 We'd add one more बराबरी to the list: पैसों के फ़ैसलों में. Equal love, equal respect, equal housework — and an equal seat when the money is decided.
drafts.why: Matches the post's Hinglish register and extends the poem's structure by one beat. Emotional post → emotional comment.

drafts.post_gist: 'One investing rule I never break' — Investing Stories #3
drafts.suggested: Ours, after teaching a few hundred beginners: never invest in anything you can't explain to your kid in one sentence. It filters out almost every mistake before it happens — complexity is where the losses hide.
drafts.why: The post invites exactly this exchange; the kid-test line is memorable and very IFM.
